quotes.text: The competent programmer is fully aware of the strictly limited size of his own skull; therefore he approaches the programming task in full humility.
quotes.author: Edsger W. Dijkstra
quotes.source: The Humble Programmer, 1972 Turing Award Lecture

quotes.text: When in doubt, use brute force.

quotes.text: C is not low level. You won't learn how memory is allocated by inspecting malloc() any more than you'd learn how characters are printed to the screen by reading printf(). You only learn about the thin or heavy wrapper that C is responsible for — the real magic is happening in the kernel and the device firmware.
quotes.author: TZubiri
quotes.source: Hacker News — What is malloc doing, anyway?
quotes.extraction_note: Classic anti-abstraction wisdom — ‘C is not low level’ is a spicy, quotable thesis; fixed capitalization and paragraph flow without changing voice.

quotes.text: It seems ridiculous that there would be consumer demand to unlock a car from a phone in the first place. What is the point of all this infrastructure and complexity? So you can be just a little bit more lazy. This sort of tech is both a vulnerability and a waste of human resources and ingenuity.
quotes.author: everdrive
quotes.source: Hacker News — Unlocking any car from X brand in most of the world
quotes.extraction_note: Pithy anti-complexity takedown — 'all this infrastructure so you can be a little more lazy' is a perfect grug-brained observation.
